# The quadratic-optimal repair also fails inverse-power convexity

This is a direct exact refinement of the already audited example in
`candidate 2439d77d03fde920`.
It tests whether the new radial-centering theorem, whose density class is
larger than log-concavity, reopens that particular repair route. It does not.

For the unique quadratic-optimal midpoint density h of that example,
on the interior vertical line parameterized by

    s=t/2+t^2/4,
    h(0,s)=4t/(1+t)^2,

put l(s)=log h(0,s). At t=2, hence s=2, exact differentiation gives

    l'(2)=-1/9,       l''(2)=1/81.

For any beta>0 set g=h^(-1/beta). Then

    g''/g=-(1/beta)l''+(1/beta^2)(l')^2,

and at the displayed interior point this equals

    (1-beta)/(81 beta^2).

It is strictly negative for EVERY beta>1. Therefore the extended
inverse-power density is not convex for any beta>1, in particular
for beta>=r+1=3 in dimension r=2. Multiplication of the density by a
normalizing constant does not change this conclusion.

The archived uniqueness argument says that every feasible midpoint law
dominating this prescribed old law in convex order must be this same
law. Thus even the relaxed promise of an inverse-power-concave
convex-order improvement in the radial theorem's class is false.
This does not claim that the law lacks a Gamma_2 center; it only closes
this proposed sufficient regularity mechanism.
